title: RoCoKV: Accelerating LLM Inference Serving through Uncertainty and Redundancy Aware KV Cache Compression
summary: RoCoKV replaces static, attention-score-based KV cache eviction for reasoning traces with uncertainty-guided adaptive pruning plus redundancy-aware token selection, delivered as fused CUDA decode kernels in a vLLM plugin that keeps the paged KV layout and CUDA graph capture. It costs implementation and maintenance complexity of a custom kernel path, reduced effective cache capacity for uncertain reasoning phases, and potential accuracy risk if confidence-based pruning miscalibrates on out-of-distribution prompts. It can fail when attention scores mislead (the paper's motivating problem), when workloads are short-output where compression overhead is not amortized, or when the plugin diverges from the reader's vLLM release and breaks CUDA graph compatibility.
rationale: The method targets exactly the reader's setting (single-GPU serving of reasoning models) and ships as a vLLM plugin, but its benefits are demonstrated only for long-chain-of-thought workloads and depend on a custom kernel that requires validation against the reader's vLLM version.
technique: Uncertainty- and redundancy-aware KV cache compression

claims.statement: RoCoKV replaces static, attention-score-based KV cache eviction for reasoning traces with uncertainty-guided adaptive pruning plus redundancy-aware token selection, delivered as fused CUDA decode kernels in a vLLM plugin that keeps the paged KV layout and CUDA graph capture. It costs implementation and maintenance complexity of a custom kernel path, reduced effective cache capacity for uncertain reasoning phases, and potential accuracy risk if confidence-based pruning miscalibrates on out-of-distribution prompts. It can fail when attention scores mislead (the paper's motivating problem), when workloads are short-output where compression overhead is not amortized, or when the plugin diverges from the reader's vLLM release and breaks CUDA graph compatibility.

For DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B in vLLM, 1.27x speedup and 38% higher throughput on AIME25, and 1.43x speedup with 45% higher throughput on a long synthetic benchmark, versus Full-KV, alongside higher accuracy than prior KV compression methods at fixed cache budgets.
